subject: Post-call action: prompt collection & model/eval recommendations for BrightLens
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightlens.ai>, Joan Park <joan.park@brightlens.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call action: prompt collection & model/eval recommendations for BrightLens

Hi Samir / Joan,

Thanks for taking the time today — really appreciate the clear breakdown of BrightLens' priority workflows (summaries for executive dashboards, classification for risk tagging, and a short-answer QA flow for analyst queries). Quick recap and requested next steps so we can scope the eval: 

Key goals we heard
- Accurate, extractive-lean summaries at 1–3 sentence length for downstream dashboards
- High-precision classification for "risk" labels (low false positives)
- Preserve provenance for any factual claims in outputs

What we need from BrightLens to run a focused model fit eval
1) Sample prompts: ~250–400 anonymized user queries and representative documents (we provide a template). Please prioritize real production queries and the edge cases you see weekly.
2) Edge-case set: 20–40 examples where your current system either fails or is unstable (hallucinations, redaction misses, ambiguous labels).
3) Redaction guidance & examples: one page that shows how you currently mask PII and PHI — we’ll apply an additional automated check and return a redaction score.

Attachments: prompt_collection_template.csv (CSV with columns and redaction hints), redaction_guidance_v1.pdf.

Model/eval expectations (quick):
- We’ll run a 2-week eval: baseline metrics (ROUGE / precision/recall for classifiers), plus a small factuality test set for hallucination rate measurement.
- Typical turnaround: we kick off after uploads + NDA updated (~1 business day).

Next steps / asks for you today
- Upload the requested files to the secure folder (link below) by EOD Friday so we can schedule the eval next week.
- Call out any compliance constraints around uploads (S3 presigned only, VPC peering, etc.).

Secure upload link (temp): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D-BRIGHTLENS-EVAL
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234564/deal/DEAL-2027-0091

If there’s anything missing from the template, tell me — we can accept CSV, JSONL, or a zipped set of examples.

Thanks,

Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- prompt_collection_template.csv (CSV, 3KB)
- redaction_guidance_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Samir Patel <samir@brightlens.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call action: prompt collection & model/eval recommendations for BrightLens

Thanks Chloe — great summary. A few clarifications before we start gathering files:

1) Redaction: we can provide de-identified reports, but can you share one short example of the redaction check you’ll run? Would like to mirror your expectations when preparing data.
2) Model recommendations: could you include a short note on models you expect to try and a rough latency/cost ballpark for the summary use case? We have strict SLAs for dashboard updates (~400ms p50).
3) Upload constraints: vendor security requires files go to our S3. We can generate a presigned URL if that works for your intake process.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if that helps.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, BrightLens
samir@brightlens.ai

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightlens.ai>, Joan Park <joan.park@brightlens.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call action: prompt collection & model/eval recommendations for BrightLens

Hi Samir — thanks for the quick note. Short answers inline, plus a couple of attachments/links so you can share with your security team.

1) Redaction check example: we run a three-step redaction assessment (pattern detection -> NLP entity scrub -> manual review sample). Example: 
   Original: "Patient John Doe, SSN 123-45-6789, presented with ..."
   Redacted: "Patient [REDACTED_NAME], SSN [REDACTED_SSN], presented with ..."
   We’ll score by redaction recall/precision and flag contextual PHI. See redaction_guidance_v1.pdf (attached).

2) Model recommendations (initial run):
   - rw-mistral-34b-q3f: lowest latency / good extractive summarization baseline (best p50 under 300ms on our hosted bench with 1K token context).
   - rw-llama-70b-q4f: stronger factuality, better for QA and longer context, expect higher cost and p50 around 600–800ms depending on instance.
   - For classification tasks we often use a distilled classifier pipeline (lightweight transformer) to hit sub-200ms p50.

   I’ve attached model_recs_and_benchmarks.pdf with sample perf numbers from similar customers and a quick cost estimate. We’ll calibrate models to your token distributions once we ingest samples.

3) Upload: presigned S3 URLs work fine — send the link plus an expiry window and we’ll pick up. If you prefer the Drive link we shared, we can accept that too.

Quality/regression notes:
- Hallucination checks: we’ll run a factuality probe (QA over source doc to detect invented facts). Expect to see initial hallucination rates 3–8% depending on model; we tune prompts and scoring to reduce that.
- Prompt drift: please include at least 50 prompts demonstrating short user edits and ambiguous queries — those drive the largest quality deltas in our evals.

Next steps:
- You send upload option (S3 presigned or Drive) + timeline.
- We ingest and run a baseline eval (2 bus. days to produce initial report).

Sharing: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D-BRIGHTLENS-EVAL
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234564/deal/DEAL-2027-0091

If useful, Aditya (cc’d) will prepare a suggested batching/latency plan to meet your p50 targets.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- model_recs_and_benchmarks.pdf (PDF, 640KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: BrightLens latency / eval ops note

Chloe — quick internal note to capture ops recommendations before we ingest: 

- If BrightLens needs ~400ms p50, start with rw-mistral-34b-q3f on Dedicated with continuous batching and a 64-token cache TTL for dashboard summaries. That should keep cost reasonable and hit p50 targets for typical doc size (~350 tokens).
- For factuality-sensitive flows (analyst QA), allocate canary traffic to rw-llama-70b-q4f; we’ll compare hallucination rates on the test set.
- Risk classification: run a two-stage flow — distilled classifier (fast) -> fallback to larger model on low-confidence labels. This reduces FPs and keeps throughput high.

Ops asks for Chloe to send to BrightLens:
1) S3 presigned URL (or Drive folder + ACL) + expiry.
2) 300 sample prompts, labeled where possible.
3) 20 edge-case examples called out in one file.

I’ll assemble a short runbook for the eval (ingest checklist, metric definitions, rollback criteria). Putting that in the HubSpot deal notes once we have their upload.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
